title: 3-Read Friday #35: Workload, Prior Knowledge, and Mini Whiteboard Pitfalls
author: Craig Barton
summary: Issue #35 links three posts on workload, prior-knowledge checking, and the limits of a favourite tool. Sam Sims argues that regular data-drop testing to track pupil progress and trigger interventions is largely a waste of teacher time given measurement error, and Barton urges senior leaders to read it. Adam Robbins identifies four reasons teachers routinely fail to explicitly check prior knowledge before teaching new material. Doug Lemov, making his second appearance in the newsletter in two weeks, catalogues potential drawbacks of overusing mini-whiteboards -- a useful corrective, Barton admits, for 'a mini-whiteboard evangelist' like himself.
points: Barton urges senior leadership teams to read Sims's workload post, calling it 'a rallying cry against the common practice of regular student testing' that wastes teacher time without improving outcomes.
He connects Robbins's four barriers to prior-knowledge checking with his own classroom observations of teachers who mention prior knowledge without ever explicitly assessing it.
He credits Lemov with a needed corrective on mini-whiteboard overuse, admitting that as 'a mini-whiteboard evangelist' himself he 'needs to read [this] once in a while.'
quotes: If your Senior Leadership Team has not read Sam’s latest post, print a copy and anonymously drop it on their desk.
It is a rallying cry against the common practice of regular student testing which aims to track pupil progress and then target interventions.
Like Adam, I regularly watch lessons where relevant prior knowledge is mentioned but not explicitly assessed.
Adam suggests four reasons why this happens and suggests strategies for ensuring the assessment of prior knowledge plays a central role in our lessons.
But I had to include this post as it discusses some potential drawbacks of overusing mini-whiteboards.
And that is something that a mini-whiteboard evangelist like myself needs to read once in a while.
